title: Finite translate enlargement with a complete original square
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. An open $U\subset Y$ in an $S$-scheme is $S$-dense if $U_s$ is dense in $Y_s$ for every $s\in S$. An $S$-rational map is a morphism on an $S$-dense open, modulo agreement on an $S$-dense common open; an $S$-birational map is represented by an isomorphism between $S$-dense opens. Smoothness and finite type have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A strict birational law on a smooth separated finite-type $S$-scheme $Y$ with nonempty fibres is an associative $S$-rational map $m:Y\times_SY\dashrightarrow Y$ for which there are opens $D,V,W\subset Y\times_SY$, each dense in every fibre of both projections to $Y$, such that $m$ is defined on $D$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(x,m(x,y))$, $(x,y)\mapsto(m(x,y),y)$ induce isomorphisms $D\simeq V$ and $D\simeq W$, respectively. Let $X\to S$ be smooth, separated, of finite type and have nonempty fibres, and let $m$ be a strict birational law on $X$. Then $X(S)\ne\varnothing$, and there exist a smooth separated finite-type $S$-scheme $Z$, an $S$-dense open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and a strict birational law $n:Z\times_SZ\dashrightarrow Z$ whose restriction to $X$ is $m$, such that $n$ has a representative defined on the entire open $j(X)\times_Sj(X)$. No everywhere-defined multiplication, inverse or identity on $Z$ is part of the conclusion.

source.place: 2.3 Proposition 5, printed pp.46-47, for sections; 5.3 construction preceding Lemma 5, Lemmas 5-7, printed pp.122-127 (PDF pp.128-133); primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the section-density lemma to $X\to S$: nonempty fibres mean surjectivity, so it gives $X(S)\ne\varnothing$. Start with $Y_0=X$, $m_0=m$, and the identity embedding of $X$. At a finite stage, if there is $a\in X(S)$ such that $\tau_a:X\dashrightarrow Y_i$ is not defined everywhere, view $a$ as a section of $Y_i$ and apply the single-translate gluing lemma to $(Y_i,m_i,a)$. Set $Y_{i+1}=Y_i^+$ and $m_{i+1}=m_i^+$. Its conclusions preserve smoothness, separatedness, finite type, nonempty fibres and the strict law. The composite embedding of $X$ stays $S$-dense: a dense open of a dense open is dense in each fibre. The new translation $\tau_a$ is defined on all of $Y_i$, hence on $X$.

source.place: 5.3 construction and Lemma 5, pp.122-124; Lemma 6, first paragraph, p.125

proof.text: For every constructed stage apply the graph-chart lemma to $(Y_i,m_i)$: let $\Gamma_i\subseteq Y_i^3$ be the schematic closure of its graph and put $Q_i=q_{12}(\Gamma_i)\cap(X\times_SX)$. The lemma makes $q_{12}(\Gamma_i)$ the maximal domain of $m_i$, with representative $q_3q_{12}^{-1}$. Hence $Q_i$ is open and is the maximal domain on the original square of the rational map $m:X\times_SX\dashrightarrow Y_i$: $m_i$ restricts to $m$, so a representative on an open of $X\times_SX$ is one on an open of $Y_i\times_SY_i$, and conversely representatives restrict. If $f$ represents $m$ into $Y_i$ on an open $O$, then $f$ followed by the open immersion $Y_i\hookrightarrow Y_{i+1}$ represents $m$ into $Y_{i+1}$ on $O$, since $m_{i+1}$ restricts to $m_i$. Thus $Q_i\subseteq Q_{i+1}$.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 6, graph closures and the increasing opens Q, p.125

proof.text: The fixed scheme $P=X\times_SX$ is Noetherian. To see finite type over $S$ explicitly, choose a finite affine cover $X=\bigcup U_b$, with $U_b=\operatorname{Spec}B_b$ and each $B_b$ a finitely generated $A$-algebra. The opens $U_b\times_SU_c=\operatorname{Spec}(B_b\otimes_AB_c)$ form a finite cover; the tensors of the two generating lists generate $B_b\otimes_AB_c$. Hence $P\to S$ is finite type. The finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma applies to $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and the closed-subset-minimal lemma shows that any increasing sequence of the $Q_i$ stabilizes: choose a minimal member among their closed complements, after which all complements are equal.

If no finite stage made every $\tau_a:X\dashrightarrow Y_i$ regular, Step 1 would recursively choose a deficient $a_{i+1}$ forever. Choose a stationary index $r$ for $Q_i$ and let $a=a_{r+1}$. In $Y_{r+1}$ the translation by $a$ has an everywhere-defined representative $f:X\to Y_{r+1}$. Let $b\in X$ lie over $s$. The continuous map $y\mapsto(a(p(y)),y,f(y))$ sends the dense set of $y$ with $(a,y)\in U$ and $f(y)=m(a,y)$ into the graph of $m$ on $U$, which lies in the closed set $\Gamma_{r+1}$ of the graph-chart lemma for $(Y_{r+1},m_{r+1})$. Hence $(a(s),b,f(b))\in\Gamma_{r+1}$ and $(a(s),b)\in q_{12}(\Gamma_{r+1})$, the maximal domain. So $(a(s),b)\in Q_{r+1}=Q_r$ for all $b\in X$, and the law with target $Y_r$ has a representative on an open containing the image of $(a\circ p,\mathrm{id}):X\to X\times_SX$. Restricting along this map gives a morphism $X\to Y_r$ equal to $m(a,\cdot)$ wherever $(a,y)\in U$, an everywhere-defined representative of $\tau_a:X\dashrightarrow Y_r$, contrary to the choice of $a$. Therefore some finite stage $Z=Y_r$, with strict law $n=m_r$, has $\tau_a:X\to Z$ defined everywhere for every $a\in X(S)$.

Write $U\subseteq X^2$ for the original strictness open. Apply the graph-chart lemma to $(X,m)$. Its projections $q_{13},q_{23}$ are open immersions with images $D=q_{13}(\Gamma)$, $E=q_{23}(\Gamma)$ dense in every fibre of both projections, so $d=q_{23}q_{13}^{-1}:D\xrightarrow{\sim}E$ is an isomorphism of opens of $X^2$. A point $(w,u,x)$ of $\Gamma$ gives $d(w,x)=(u,x)$, i.e. $d(w,x)=(w^{-1}x,x)$ with $w^{-1}x$ the lemma's left division. Consider $F=\{(w,x,y):(w,x)\in D,\ (w^{-1}x,y)\in U\}\subseteq X^3$. It is open and dense in every fibre of $p_{23}:X^3\to X^2$. Indeed fix $(x,y)$ over a residue field $L$: the change of variable $w\mapsto u=w^{-1}x$ is an isomorphism between dense opens of $X_L$, using the second-projection density of $D,E$. The condition $(u,y)\in U_L$ is dense open by the second-projection strictness of $U$ and its base-change density. Its intersection with that dense image is dense; pulling it back gives a dense open in the $w$-fibre.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 6, open set Z in the proof (called F here), p.126

proof.text: Let $t\in X^2$ lie over $s$, $L=\kappa(t)$. Step 5 makes $F_t$ a dense open of $X_L$; the section-density lemma gives $a\in X(S)$ with $(a_L,t)\in F_t$. On the open neighbourhood $N_a$ of $t$ cut out by $(a,x)\in D$ and $(a^{-1}x,y)\in U$, $h_a(x,y)=\tau_a(m(a^{-1}x,y))$ is a morphism to $Z$: division and $m|_U$ are morphisms there, and Step 4 gives $\tau_a:X\to Z$. It represents $n$ on $N_a$. Let $W\subseteq X^3$ be the open of $(p,u,y)$ with $(u,y),(p,u),(p,uy),(pu,y)\in U$; there $p(uy)$ and $(pu)y$ are morphisms, equal on an $S$-dense, hence dense, open by associativity. $X^3$ is reduced and locally Noetherian by smooth reduced pullback and base change, as in Step 7; that dense open of the Noetherian $W$ is schematically dense by the reduced-dense-image lemma, and the separated-target lemma gives $p(uy)=(pu)y$ on all of $W$. Its slice $p=a$, written in $x=au$, is the open of $N_a$ where also $(a,u)$ and $(a,uy)$ lie in $U$. It meets every fibre of $N_a\to X$ over $y$ in a dense open: each condition is dense in $u$ by strictness of $U$ and the fibrewise isomorphisms $u\mapsto au$, $u\mapsto uy$, and Step 5 transports it to $x$. Projections of fibres being open, this slice is dense in each $S$-fibre of $N_a$. On it $h_a(x,y)=a((a^{-1}x)y)=(a(a^{-1}x))y=xy$, using $m(a,a^{-1}x)=x$ from the graph-chart lemma. These neighbourhoods cover $X^2$.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 6, choice of a section and formula a((a^{-1}x)y), p.126

proof.text: The local representatives from Step 6 agree on overlaps. For precision, $S$ is reduced and locally Noetherian (normal local rings are domains); smooth reduced pullback first makes $X$ reduced and locally Noetherian. The strict-law-base-change node makes $X^2\to X$ smooth as a base change of $X\to S$, and a second smooth reduced pullback makes $X^2$ reduced and locally Noetherian. Each overlap is an open of the Noetherian scheme $X^2$, and two representatives agree on a dense open by their rational equality. That dense open immersion is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, since its source and the overlap are Noetherian. The reduced-dense-image lemma makes it schematically dense. The separated-target equality lemma, with target $Z\to S$, now gives equality on the whole overlap. Scheme morphism gluing produces a single $X^2\to Z$. It represents $n$ everywhere on the original square, which is the requested conclusion with $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$. All the asserted properties of $Z,j,n$ were retained in Step 1; the construction uses only finitely many translation gluings.

source.place: 5.3 Lemma 6, end of proof, p.126; explicit separated gluing of local representatives

proof_origin.place: BLR 5.3 Lemma 6, pp.125-126, assembled from Lemmas 3-5 and 7; online primary scan read; local PDF WANTED. The stabilization and pointwise associativity argument is written out, with explicit separated gluing.
